questions.q: Why can't an INNER JOIN between POZ_SUPPLIERS and AP_INVOICES_ALL ever answer "which suppliers have zero invoices"?
options: INNER JOIN only works on numeric columns
INNER JOIN drops any supplier row with no matching invoice row before a WHERE clause even runs
INNER JOIN always returns every supplier regardless of invoices
POZ_SUPPLIERS cannot be joined to AP_INVOICES_ALL at all
questions.explain: By definition INNER JOIN only keeps matched rows, so a supplier with no invoices is excluded entirely — exactly the rows this question needs.

questions.q: What does `LEFT OUTER JOIN` do differently from `INNER JOIN`?
options: It only returns rows that match on both sides, same as INNER JOIN
It keeps every row from the right-hand table only
It keeps every row from the left-hand table, filling unmatched right-side columns with NULL
It removes duplicate rows automatically
questions.explain: LEFT OUTER JOIN preserves every row from the left table even when there's no match on the right, using NULL for the unmatched side's columns.

questions.q: In `... LEFT OUTER JOIN ap_invoices_all i ON s.vendor_id = i.vendor_id WHERE i.invoice_id IS NULL`, what does the WHERE clause isolate?
options: Suppliers that have at least one invoice
Invoices with a NULL invoice amount
Every row in the result, since IS NULL always matches everything
Suppliers with zero matching invoice rows — i.invoice_id is only NULL when there was no match
questions.explain: After a LEFT OUTER JOIN, the right table's key column is NULL only for rows that found no match — isolating suppliers with no invoices.

questions.q: What is the legacy `(+)` notation used for in Oracle SQL, as in `WHERE s.vendor_id = i.vendor_id (+)`?
options: It is Oracle's pre-ANSI outer join syntax, placed on the side that may be missing a match
It performs addition on the join column
It forces an INNER JOIN instead of an outer join
It is a comment marker with no functional effect
questions.explain: The (+) symbol is Oracle's older, non-ANSI way of marking an outer join; this course prefers ANSI LEFT OUTER JOIN but you should recognize (+) in legacy code.

questions.q: Why does this course recommend LEFT OUTER JOIN over the legacy (+) syntax going forward?
options: Because (+) is no longer supported by any version of Oracle
Because LEFT OUTER JOIN is harder to read
Because (+) is easier to misplace, silently changing which side is kept, while LEFT OUTER JOIN is clearer and ANSI-standard
There is no real reason — both are equally recommended
questions.explain: LEFT OUTER JOIN is the clearer, ANSI-standard approach; (+) still works in Oracle but is more error-prone to write correctly.
